subject: Clarify: rerank/classifier SKU and how scoring is billed
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@finlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-03-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rerank/classifier pricing question

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We have a couple of evaluation threads running and our engineering lead asked a straightforward question: how are rerank/classifier endpoints billed on the hosted API? Specifically:

- Do you charge per API call or per candidate scored?
- Are there separate token charges for the context/queries we send?
- What does the baseline rate card look like for scoring-heavy workloads?

I've attached a small sample of the candidate sets (Finlytics_Rerank_Example.csv) so you can see our typical fanout (~50 candidates per user query, avg. candidate text length ~120 tokens).

Also curious about packaging: is this covered under standard hosted usage or do we need a Dedicated SKU to get predictable unit economics?

Can you send a short example calculation so our SREs can model costs?

Best,
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Finlytics

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rerank/classifier pricing question

Alex — thanks for the sample, this is helpful. Short answers up front, then a worked example.

1) Billing model (hosted API rerank/classifier): we bill two components for scoring-heavy endpoints:
   - Scoring units: a per-candidate "score" fee (you pay once for each candidate the model scores).
   - Token usage: the model context (prompt + candidates + any system instructions) is billed under per-token usage like other API calls.

2) Why both? The scoring unit captures per-candidate compute (lightweight replicated scoring), and token billing captures the cost of sending large candidate contexts and any instruction/metadata.

3) Packaging: you can run on the normal hosted tier and get usage-based billing, or commit to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput and a lower per-score price (monthly reserved fee + reduced per-score unit).

Worked example using your sample numbers:
- Fanout: 50 candidates per query
- Avg candidate length: 120 tokens
- Prompt overhead (user query + system instruction): 80 tokens

Assume baseline list prices (hosted):
- Scoring unit: $0.0012 per candidate scored
- Token price: $0.45 per 1M tokens (aggregate of context+responses)

Per-query math:
- Scoring cost: 50 candidates * $0.0012 = $0.06
- Token count: 50 * 120 (candidates) + 80 (prompt) = 6,080 tokens ~ 0.00608 of a million
- Token cost: 0.00608 * $0.45 = $0.002736
- Total per query: $0.062736 (~$0.063)

If you run 100k queries/day at this fanout, monthly cost (30d) ~ 100k * 30 * $0.063 = $189,000.

Discounting and dedicated pricing:
- Committed monthly scoring volume reduces the per-score fee (we typically offer tiered discounts at 20% for >=1M scores/month, 30% for >=3M/month with 12-month commitment).
- Dedicated pools provide further per-score reductions but include a monthly reserved fee (depends on size and SLO).

I'll pull the current Q1 PDF rate card and a quick committed-pricing sketch and send it in a follow-up. If you'd like, we can also run a short cost-sensitivity calc with your expected monthly traffic and fanout.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

2) Would you be willing to provide a 12-month committed pricing proposal? We're aiming to get predictable unit economics for forecasting.

Also one more: if we use cascade/rerank approach (cheap filter model then a heavier classifier on the top N), how is that billed — do we pay for every stage's scoring?

Attached is the sample CSV we mentioned.

Thanks — Alex

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-03-05T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Rerank/classifier pricing question — Finlytics (need discount guidance)

Short answer on cascade: we bill each model invocation (each scoring call). If you configure a cascade that filters 90% of candidates at stage 1, you will only pay scoring units for stage 1 on all candidates and stage 2 for the top N you pass through. So total cost = sum of each stage's scored candidates * the stage's per-score price + token usage across stages.

Notes:
- We offer a "cascade discount" in committed deals where we can price the lightweight filter model at a reduced scorable-unit rate (because it's cheaper to run).
- Quantization/engine tuning does not change the billing units — only the per-score price we can offer if you commit to Dedicated.

Marcus — from product side, recommending we provide a staged pricing sheet: baseline per-score, cascade adjusted per-score for stage 1, stage 2, and dedicated pool option.

—Eve

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Rerank/classifier pricing question — Finlytics (need discount guidance)

FYI on discount bands: without VP approval AEs can commit up to a 20% discount on list price for annual agreements. For something at ~375M scored units/month we should be routing to Commercial/VP for deeper concessions — I'd be comfortable recommending 22–28% contingent on committed monthly volume and an MRR floor. Also require a 60-day SLA review for Dedicated pricing.

If you want to move fast, propose a formal 22% discount and flag for escalation — I'll prepare the finance justification pack.

—Marcus
